newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan extra budget seen more likely after tankan.
newsitem.headline: Japan extra budget seen more likely after tankan.

text.p: Japan is more likely to have to put together a supplementary budget for the fiscal year to March 31, 1997, after the Bank of Japan's tankan survey showed worsening corporate sentiment, economists said on Wednesday.

"Public works projects will subside...and the consumption tax (rise) will have a negative impact next year, so the Diet (parliament) will feel forced to accommodate the needs of the economy in some way," said Tadashi Kiuchi, chief economist at the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan.
"Special income tax cuts or some small supplementary budget may be the subject of discussion," he added.

Robert Feldman, chief economist at Salomon Brothers Asia, agreed. "Certainly there is increased certainty (of a supplementary budget). The debate over whether to do it at all will obviously be tilted in favour of doing it," he said.

Economic Planning Agency Minister Shusei Tanaka told a news conference on Tuesday that the government would decide if extra fiscal spending was necessary to keep the economic recovery on track after looking at key data, including the tankan.
He said he still felt the government should not easily rely on fiscal spending, but that there was room for debate on steps such as continuing special tax cuts after looking at the data.
